defects.description: Look-ahead / fail-open on future-dated snapshots. fair() picks max(obs_ms) and clamps age with max(0, now_ms - obs_ms), and continuous_sources() keeps any record with now_ms - obs_ms <= max_age (negative ages pass). A snapshot observed after now_ms is therefore used as perfectly fresh. Probe: a sharp snapshot at now+1h is chosen over one at now-2h with age 0 and sigma=s0, and a Kalshi record at now+1h alone makes quote_allowed return (True,'ok'). Live, this only matters under clock skew or a misparsed vendor timestamp, but such a snapshot then disables the max_age refusal and the pulls' 'no fresh sharp reference' and lineup checks for that event. In a Loop B replay, checkpoint_rows(…, ts_ms) would use prices from after ts_ms and bias the pre-registered Brier/log-loss guardrail. No current AC requires as-of filtering and no replay caller exists yet, so this is minor.
defects.fix_hint: In fair() and continuous_sources(), ignore records with obs_ms > now_ms (or recv_ms > now_ms for replay availability), e.g. add `and s['obs_ms'] <= now_ms` to the filters, and add one test case.

defects.description: A sticky caution pull (resume_requires_fresh_observation=True) also ends when a later 'shrink' signal, or a later non-sticky 'pull' that then expires, arrives for the same (role, scope). The probe [sticky, shrink] returned []. The dispatch says it ends only when replaced by action 'none'. WP4-D's sentinel only emits sticky 'pull' or 'none', so this cannot happen today.
defects.fix_hint: When the current signal for (role, scope) is not 'none' and an earlier signal in that key was a sticky pull, keep the pull, i.e. only an action=='none' signal clears a sticky pull.
